title: Adversaries themselves confess Moses' and Christ's miracles; Jews invent magic or the Name
pass_a_gloss: But besides, true to-be what done are-reported by Moses miracles, and likewise those which are-attributed to-Christ and to-his Apostles, from the-adversaries'-own confession is-clear. For what to Christ pertains, the-Jews who are of-the-Christian name enemies most-hostile, neither formerly dared, nor even-now dare to-deny Christ to-have-performed miracles: but I-know-not what they-have-invented, that they-may-elude the-force of-the-argument which therefrom we-draw; namely either Christ those-things to-have-done by-magic art, which in Egypt he-had-learned: or by-virtue of-that name the-tetragrammaton, whose right pronunciation and exposition he-was-holding. For they-fable that whoever that name knows rightly to-pronounce, to-be-able by-force of-that name any works wonderful to-do. Of-which invention the-vanity through itself is-clear, nor need there-is it to-refute. Only here we-note not a-little therefrom to-be-confirmed the-truth of-Christ's miracles: since the-Jews who most his glory envy, not dare, nor are-able openly to-deny those-things done to-have-been. And likewise of-the-Gentiles very-many testimony to-Moses bore, and the-truth acknowledged of-the-Mosaic history, as to-be-seen is in the-books of-Josephus against Apion, and of-Eusebius on the-preparation of-the-Gospel.
pass_b_english: But besides, that the miracles reported as done by Moses are true, and likewise those attributed to Christ and his Apostles, is clear from the adversaries' own confession. For as to Christ, the Jews who are most hostile enemies of the Christian name neither formerly dared, nor even now dare, to deny that Christ performed miracles: but they have invented I know not what to elude the force of the argument we draw therefrom — namely either that Christ did those things by magic art which he had learned in Egypt, or by virtue of that tetragrammaton Name whose right pronunciation and exposition he held. For they fable that whoever knows how to pronounce that name rightly can by its force do any wonderful works. The vanity of that invention is clear of itself, and there is no need to refute it. Here we only note that the truth of Christ's miracles is not a little confirmed thereby: since the Jews who most envy his glory neither dare nor are able openly to deny that those things were done. And likewise very many of the Gentiles bore testimony to Moses and acknowledged the truth of the Mosaic history, as is to be seen in the books of Josephus against Apion, and of Eusebius on the Preparation of the Gospel.
source_text: XXV. Sed praeterea vera esse quae facta perhibentur a Mose miracula, et similiter ea quae tribuuntur Christo et Apostolis ejus, ex ipsa adversariorum confessione patet. Nam quod ad Christum attinet, Judaei qui sunt Christiani nominis hostes infestissimi, nec olim ausi sunt, nec etiamnum audent negare Christum patrasse miracula: sed nescio quid commenti sunt, ut eludant vim argumenti quod inde deducimus; nempe vel Christum illa fecisse arte magica, quam in Aegypto didicerat: vel virtute nominis illius tetragrammati, cujus rectam pronunciationem et expositionem tenebat. Fabulantur enim quicunque nomen illud scit recte pronunciare, posse vi illius nominis quavis opera miranda facere. Cujus commenti vanitas per se patet, nec opus est illud refutare. Solummodo hic notamus non parum inde confirmari veritatem miraculorum Christi: quandoquidem Judaei qui maxime ejus gloriae invident, non audent, neque possunt aperte negare illa facta fuisse. Et similiter Ethnicorum plurimi testimonium Mosi perhibuerunt, et veritatem agnoverunt historiae Mosaicae, ut videre est in libris Josephi contra Appionem, et Eusebii de praeparatione Evangelica.
